I have been working this land for 25 years, and at 54 I know what my two-person household can handle. My husband works part-time off the farm in town, so I manage the day-to-day field work, though he comes back for the busy harvest and planting windows. We have 24 mu in total and our own well, so I can irrigate when I need to, but I still watch the electricity costs. Wheat and maize are my backbone—I trust the wheat-maize double-cropping system because it is mechanized, the buyers come to the village, and it gives us two harvests a year. I will put 20 mu into that rotation. The wheat went in last October with an improved variety, and this spring I will irrigate it four times—green-up, jointing, heading and grain filling—and spray three times for weeds and aphids. After wheat harvest in early June, I will plant hybrid maize directly into the stubble with no-tillage to save time and labor; it needs three irrigations and three pesticide applications for armyworm and weeds. I keep 4 mu of cotton because I have grown it since I was young and the income is good when prices hold, but it is labor-intensive, so I limit it to what I can manage. I will rotary-till the cotton field in spring, plant hybrid cotton in late April, irrigate it four times, and spray about ten times for bollworm and aphids. I expect around 550 kg per mu of wheat, 650 kg per mu of maize, and about 300 kg per mu of seed cotton if the season is normal.
